spec_cite: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §5.2 (CONNECTING: capacity exceeded -> transport close carrying 301)
docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §10 (32 established sessions, TM-2; 16 concurrent handshakes, TM-1)
description: Server at capacity: the connection is refused BEFORE any control frame exists — signaled ONLY by the QUIC application close code 301 (no Error frame, no Close frame).
preconditions: State machine: CONNECTING; the Server is at its established-session limit (default 32) or handshake limit (16).
This is the transport-close-only signaling mode named by the §5.2 row — there is no control stream exchange at all.

steps.note: No control frames are sent or expected; the QUIC application close carries code 301.

assertions: Expected control-stream bytes: NONE. The only observable is the transport close with code 301.
Client policy (spec §6.3): 301 is retryable -> reconnect with backoff (1 s base, ×2, 30 s cap, ±20% jitter).
Contrast with error-602, which DOES send a Close frame — some failure modes signal only via the transport close code, others via frames; the §5.2 rows decide which.
